newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North sees neat fit with iron ore buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North sees neat fit with iron ore buy.

text.p: North Ltd said on Friday its purchase of a controlling interest in Canada's largest iron ore pellet producer will provide access to a growing market that doesn't compete with its existing iron ore business.
North manages Robe River Iron Associates in the Pilbara region of Western Australia and said earlier on Friday it will pay US$230 million for 59.3 percent of Iron Ore Co of Canada.

North also said in a statement it would be investigating potential development of the higher grade West Angela iron ore deposit in the Pilbara as well as searching for new acquisitions in other parts of the world.
"This purchase will complement our interest in Robe River and positions North as major player in the world's iron ore industry," North managing director Campbell Anderson said.

North said the Canadian company was attractive because it had a 20-year life in current resrves, with the potential to access substantial additional reserves and well established markets in North America and Europe.
The acquisition would have an immediate impact on North's earnings and return on capital, North said.

The acquisition would also provide North with an opportunity to capitalise on fast-growing electric arc furnace, or mini-mill, steel markets in the U.S. and Asia via reactivating an idle pellet plant at Sept-lles in Quebec province.
Iron ore pellets are used as supplementary feed for electric arc furnace steelmaking.
The Sept-Lles plant has stockpile capacity of 5.5 million tonnes and is located on a deep-water port capable of loading ships up to 220,000 DWT in capapcity, North said.
Iron Ore Co produces over 15 million tonnes a year of iron ore pellets and concentrates and employs over 2,400 people.
Iron Ore Co's North America sales would continue to be made under long term contracts, primarily with Bethlehem Steel Co National Steel Co and Dofasco Inc

The purchase of IOCC shares, comprising the combination of Bethlehem Steel's 37.6 percent held by Bethlehem Steel and 21.7 percent by National Steel, is subject to regulatory and government approvals and the consents of the remaining shareholders, Mitsubishi Corp, with 21.8 percent, Dofasco Inc 6.9 percent, and the Labrador Iron Ore Royalty Income Fund 12 percent, North said.
The deal was expected to be finalised by the end of the first quarter of calendar 1997.
Under the agreement, Bethlehem would receive about US$145 million and National would receive around US$85 million.
